content_preview.title: Gleam 1.19.0 Compiles to Erlang Abstract Format Instead of Erlang Source and Flattens JavaScript Pattern Matching; 1.19.1 Followed Two Days Later
content_preview.summary: Gleam 1.19.0, dated October 5, 2026, replaces textual Erlang output with Erlang abstract forms; v1.19.1, dated October 7, fixes the export prelude commands.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Gleam project published v1.19.0 of its compiler on 5 October 2026. In the release post on the [Gleam project blog](https://gleam.run/news/gleam-doesnt-compile-to-erlang-source-anymore/), Louis Pilfold writes that previously Gleam generated Erlang source code and now generates Erlang abstract forms. The [project changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gleam-lang/gleam/v1.19.0/CHANGELOG.md) heads the release "1.19.0 - 2026-10-05" and lists its entries under the release candid...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece (Overview, Erlang back end, JS/TS output, build tools and warnings, patch release, What We Don't Know). Body is 808 words raw and 808 with link URLs stripped (News range 400-1200). Title is 145 characters (cap 150). Summary 156 characters. No policy violations. Title wording 'Erlang Abstract Format' is the changelog's phrase (rc1 entry: 'compiles to the Erlang Abstract Format instead of textual Erlang'); the blog itself says 'Erlang abstract forms' and 'Gleam doesn't compile to Erlang source anymore'. The title is an unquoted paraphrase supported by the combined sources, not a defect.
editor_notes.source_verification: Integrity: submission file confirmed by title from origin/<PR branch> via git show (PR has exactly one file, no strays); hash and Ed25519 signature valid per chief:review; all three snapshots exist with HTTP 200 and I re-hashed each decompressed file against the manifest sha256 (all match). suspicious_patterns is null for all three sources; no injection text found. source-0.html.gz (gleam.run release post, 'Gleam v1.19.0 released!', 05 October, 2026 by Louis Pilfold): full page body present. Confirms: Cavalieri rewrote the Erlang code generator over the last few months; 'Previously Gleam generated Erlang source code, now it generates Erlang abstract forms'; abstract forms are an IR that lets Gleam skip the front half of the Erlang compiler; location metadata accurate to Gleam source, 'perfectly accurate' stacktrace line numbers, previously 'only pointing to the nearest function'; edb remark with 'we have not done any work on this ourselves'; langcompilebench by Jose Valim, 100 modules x 100 functions returning 'hello world', v1.17.0 vs v1.19.0, first stage in v1.18.0; benchmarks 'contrived' and 'insufficient to draw any hard conclusions'; BEAM bytecode not fixed; Elixir also compiles via abstract forms; Downey flatter JS pattern matching and 'little-to-no change' to minified size; short list literals use prepend(...)/empty instead of arrayToList, 'especially impactful' for Lustre, no improvement recorded for longer lists, credited to Cavalieri; TypeScript overload (stop generalisation to unknown); Rodrigo Alvarez build-tool changes (--no-dev, .app files, stdout export, intent of Mix/rebar3 support); Alistair Smith label support; Downey format_source in the Wasm build; export javascript-prelude/typescript-prelude can write to a file. The chart values are SVG axis labels only (0ms-500ms, 0ms-1000ms) with no data values in text; the article states no timing numbers and correctly says so. source-1.html.gz (raw CHANGELOG.md at v1.19.0): heading '## 1.19.0 - 2026-10-05' is empty and entries sit under 1.19.0-rc1 (2026-09-22), rc2 (2026-09-26), rc3 (2026-10-01), exactly as the article says. Confirms: compile times reduced for a typical package; '[..x] -> x' warning with 'This syntax may be removed in a future (major) release.'; empty-string bit array segments deprecated; overlapping-string unreachable warning with 'Code that previously compiled cleanly may now emit this warning.'; Record -> record_ rename for OTP29's built-in record type; '--src-only' renamed '--no-dev'; --otp-app-names flag; TypeScript overload example Box$isFull<I>(value: Box$<I>): value is Full<I>. source-2.html.gz (raw CHANGELOG.md at v1.19.1, 311 bytes): '## v1.19.1 - 2026-10-07', one bug fix: export javascript-prelude and export typescript-prelude commands would not run. All quote-marked strings in the article ('1.19.0 - 2026-10-05', 'may be removed in a future (major) release', 'Code that previously compiled cleanly may now emit this warning.', 'hello world') are verbatim. JS snippets: the blog uses isWibble(x), the changelog uses x instanceof Wibble; the article reproduces neither and flags the discrepancy in What We Don't Know, which is accurate. Title claim 'Followed Two Days Later': blog dated 5 October; 1.19.0 changelog heading 2026-10-05; v1.19.1 changelog heading 2026-10-07. The article attributes the 1.19.1 date explicitly to the tag changelog ('is dated 2026-10-07') and the 1.19.0 date to the blog and changelog heading. Independently cross-checked via GitHub API (not a cited source): release v1.19.0 published_at 2026-10-05T17:01:45Z, v1.19.1 2026-10-07T20:23:35Z, so the two-day gap holds. (GitHub shows rc3 published 2026-10-02 vs changelog 2026-10-01; the article cites the changelog date and attributes it to the changelog.) Attribution: blog-only claims (stacktrace accuracy, list literals, Mix/rebar3 intent, edb, JS flattening) are attributed to the blog; changelog-only items (--no-dev rename, Record rename, warnings) are attributed to the changelog. The article's description that --no-dev 'is a rename of --src-only' follows the changelog; note that --src-only appears in the same rc1 cycle, so it never shipped in a stable release, which the article does not claim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No unsupported numbers, names or dates. Every specific traces to the three snapshots. Vendor claims (compile-time improvement, 'perfectly accurate' stacktraces, 'especially impactful' list change) are attributed to the Gleam project and the article states the benchmark is the project's own and that no independent measurement was among the sources. The statement that the 1.19.1 fix 'concerns a command area touched in 1.19.0' is a modest inference, tied to the blog's sentence that those commands gained the ability to write to a file; it is flagged as such by wording and is supported.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Praise present in the blog ('nice improvement', 'excellent') is not reproduced. No AI self-reference. Mildly informal 'What We Don't Know' heading is consistent with house style.
editor_notes.originality: Earlier Gleam coverage exists for 1.16 (2026-04/30) and 1.17 (2026-06/06); none for 1.18 or 1.19. This article covers a new release and a distinct topic. Related article links added in article-meta. Article contains no internal links, so no link-gate risk. gleam.run is already in config/source_allowlist.txt (line 1717, added with the Gleam 1.17 article) and raw.githubusercontent.com is at line 1679; no allowlist changes needed.
concerns: Blog and changelog show different JavaScript snippets (isWibble(x) vs instanceof Wibble); the article acknowledges this and reproduces neither.
The 1.19.0 changelog heading is empty and its entries sit under rc1-rc3; the article says so explicitly.
Release dates for 1.19.1 rest on the tag changelog heading; corroborated by the GitHub API but not by a cited source.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed release coverage resting entirely on the Gleam project's own pages, with appropriate caveats about the vendor benchmark. Approved without corrections.
